title: Black Diamond Korea says outsourced ERP server was breached, customer data may have leaked
date_note: Date of the company's public notice (20 November, 2:25 p.m.); its ERP provider found signs of intrusion on 19 November, per the Dailysecu report.
geo_basis: country as stated in the source; no city given
summary: Black Diamond Korea said its external ERP service provider, which handles order and shipping operations, showed signs of a server intrusion on 19 November. In a notice on 20 November the company said customer names, mobile numbers, shipping addresses and order history may have leaked, and that it has not yet confirmed data left the system. It reported the incident to KISA and says shipping is delayed.
plain: An outdoor-brand retailer in Korea says a breach at its order-system supplier may have exposed customers' names, phone numbers, addresses and order history. It has not confirmed a leak.
exec: A supplier breach may have exposed customer contact and order data at a consumer brand, and shipping is delayed.
action: Customers: be wary of text messages and emails posing as Black Diamond or couriers, avoid links and app-install prompts in delivery messages; the company says it never asks for passwords, account numbers or authentication codes.
impact: Name, mobile number, shipping address and order history of member and non-member customers of the online mall possibly exposed; number of customers not disclosed.

validation.note: Dailysecu report relaying the company's notice; the company's own notice page was not read and no second publisher found.
